d: The Executive Director, Utilities leads the City Operations utilities mandate across Qiddiya City, covering power, potable water, renewed water, wastewater, stormwater, ICT, water bodies, lagoons and other utility systems within scope. The role is accountable for improving the operational management and resilience of existing interim networks, water bodies and lagoons; protecting continuity of service during construction; defining the city-wide utilities strategy, ownership model and operating standards; and ensuring permanent utility and water assets are planned, designed, delivered and accepted in line with City Operations and Qiddiya City Authority requirements. Reporting to the City Chief Operations Officer, the role coordinates closely with planning, design, delivery, district and asset teams, QTech, Smart City, utility providers, regulators and O&M partners to manage material service, capacity, water-quality, commercial and reputational risks.

Develop and implement the City Operations strategy for all utilities, water bodies and lagoons, including service outcomes, water quality, resilience, governance, ownership, operating and cost model, standards and long-term investment priorities.

Determine which interim and permanent utility assets will be adopted by City Operations and which will be owned or operated by utilities, districts, assets or other third parties, with clear decision rights and accountability.
Improve the operational management, asset information, condition oversight and service performance of existing interim power, potable water, renewed water and ICT networks.

Develop and implement a protection and continuity strategy for live interim utility networks during construction, recognising that outages create a material operational and reputational risk for Qiddiya.
Maintain an accurate city-wide utilities asset register and GIS record, including surveys of existing interim networks and requirements for any relocation arising from development works.
Advise the City Chief Operations Officer and governance on utility priorities, delivery dependencies, capacity constraints, temporary solutions, investment needs and material operational risks.
Coordinate with planning, design and delivery teams to accelerate permanent utility assets needed for growing city-wide operational, development and major-event requirements.
Define City Operations requirements and assure their incorporation into utility strategies, project briefs, designs, specifications, delivery plans and permanent-asset operating models.

Verify that interim and full-build infrastructure can meet peak utility loads, including concurrent major-event scenarios and increased city footfall, with adequate redundancy and recovery arrangements.

Lead operational assurance of critical dependencies and interfaces, including permanent and temporary power, potable and renewed water capacity, wastewater, stormwater, water bodies and lagoons, utility corridors, ICT connectivity and data-centre requirements.
Coordinate space planning for utility operational centres, O&M yards, workshops and equipment and spare-parts storage, confirming the required number, location and functionality across Qiddiya City.
Participate in multidisciplinary stage-gate reviews and challenge solutions to optimise safety, service continuity, maintainability, whole-life cost, efficiency and operational readiness.

Establish utility readiness, testing, commissioning, handover and operational acceptance requirements, including permits, asset data, GIS records, operating procedures, warranties, spares, training and defect closure.
Assess acceptance evidence and recommend City Operations acceptance only where ownership, operating responsibility, funding and service interfaces are clear.

Aggregate city-wide O&M requirements and lead the technical and operational strategy for a multi-year city-wide utilities O&M services procurement, coordinating with Commercial, Procurement, Finance and Legal.

Coordinate mobilisation and transition arrangements for interim and permanent networks, including temporary service extensions where delays to permanent assets require continued use of temporary power, water or ICT solutions.
Ensure adopted assets are captured in the asset management system and GIS with complete, accurate and usable information for safe operation and maintenance.

Establish KPIs and executive reporting for availability, outages, reliability, water quality, water-body and lagoon condition, capacity, losses, consumption, compliance, incidents, cost, complaints and recovery performance.

Maintain a consolidated utilities risk and dependency register covering delivery slippage, temporary-network fragility, corridor and land constraints, capacity shortfalls, construction interfaces and unbudgeted temporary solutions.
Develop lifecycle, renewal and investment plans based on criticality, condition, service demand, resilience, regulatory requirements and whole-life value.

Confirm the operational data required for smart utilities, align the Siemens utilities integration study with QTech and Smart City initiatives, and define requirements for monitoring, analytics and future digital-twin capability.
Ensure emergency, outage, business continuity and recovery plans are coordinated with City Operations, districts, assets, utility providers, safety, security and event functions.

Define the utilities cost-recovery model, including cost allocation, metering, tariffs or charges, billing inputs, subsidy requirements, subsidy period and governance for costs levied on operational assets.

Lead the utility component of the city service charge in collaboration with the Executive Director, City Asset Management and Finance and Control, ensuring transparent and auditable recovery mechanisms.

Draft and implement service level agreements between City Operations and districts or assets for utilities adopted by City Operations, including service standards, responsibilities, escalation, outage communication and performance reporting.
Develop City Operations codes, standards and guidelines for construction in the vicinity of live utility assets, including permits, protection measures, access controls and incident response.
Manage strategic interfaces with authorities, regulators, Saudi Electricity, water entities, telecoms providers, developers, districts, operators and specialist O&M service providers.
Ensure statutory, technical, environmental, commercial and contractual obligations are identified, governed and evidenced across all adopted utilities.
Build and lead a capable municipal utilities team with clear accountability, effective governance and disciplined delivery.
Develop Saudi talent through structured recruitment, mentoring, role exposure, succession planning and knowledge transfer from advisers, delivery partners and operators.
Promote collaboration, technical rigour, commercial discipline, innovation and continuous improvement.
q: Bachelor's degree in engineering, utilities, infrastructure, asset management or a related discipline.
Postgraduate qualification in engineering, asset management, business or a related field is advantageous.
Relevant professional registration or accreditation in engineering, utilities, asset management or project management is preferred.

Substantial executive leadership experience in city-wide utilities, infrastructure asset management or utility network development within a complex city, municipality, mixed-use destination or major development programme.
Demonstrated experience managing live interim or temporary utility networks while permanent infrastructure is planned and delivered in an active construction environment.
Strong experience across utility strategy, planning, design assurance, construction interfaces, testing, commissioning, handover, operational acceptance and service mobilisation.
Proven experience in network resilience, outage management, peak-demand planning, lifecycle investment, GIS and asset information, operational data and regulatory compliance.
Demonstrated experience developing utility O&M procurement strategies, SLAs, performance regimes, tariffs, metering, billing, cost-recovery or subsidy models.

Proven ability to manage interfaces among developers, delivery teams, authorities, regulators, utilities, districts, operators and service providers; experience in Saudi Arabia or the wider GCC is strongly preferred.
Expert understanding of city-wide utility asset management, live-network operations and governance of networked infrastructure.

d: We are seeking a Red Hat Linux Administrator with strong hands-on experience in RHEL server administration, OS patching, hardening, environment configuration, and production support. The ideal candidate will be responsible for maintaining the availability, performance, security, and reliability of Linux environments across development, testing, and production.
Administer and support Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) servers across enterprise environments.
Perform OS installation, configuration, patching, upgrades, and system hardening .
Monitor server health, performance, capacity, and availability, and troubleshoot system-level issues.
Manage users, groups, permissions, services, filesystems, processes, and system configurations.
Support production environments and participate in incident, problem, and change management activities.
Implement security best practices, vulnerability remediation, and configuration standards.
Automate routine administrative tasks using Shell scripting and/or Ansible .
Maintain technical documentation, operational procedures, and system configuration records.
4–6 years of hands-on experience in Linux system administration, preferably in enterprise production environments.
Strong expertise in Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) administration and troubleshooting.
Good understanding of Linux networking, filesystems, storage, DNS, SSH, systemd, processes, and permissions .
Experience with OS patching, server hardening, vulnerability remediation, and configuration management .
Hands-on experience with Shell scripting and/or Ansible .
Familiarity with monitoring, logging, backup, and enterprise infrastructure tools.
Experience working in 24x7 production support environments and following ITIL-based operational processes.
Strong analytical, troubleshooting, communication, and incident-management skills.
RHCSA/RHCE certification or equivalent experience will be an advantage.
